caption.text:
Another carriage horse has died in Central Park.

His name was Deniz.  According to NYPD officials, he was sixteen years old and was pulling a carriage carrying two passengers when he collapsed.

Officers who spoke with the driver reported that the horse appeared to suffer a medical emergency.

The cause of Deniz’s death remains unknown pending a necropsy, and authorities have stated there is no indication of criminality at this time.

While horses commonly live well into their twenties, and many reach their late twenties or even thirties, Deniz died at sixteen years old on the streets of Manhattan while working as a carriage horse.

Every horse deserves our respect and compassion.  Horses are athletes, companions, working animals, and trusted partners.

While the circumstances surrounding Deniz’s death have not yet been determined, his passing once again raises important questions about the continued use of horse-drawn carriages in one of the busiest and most congested urban environments in the world.

The Wild Beauty Foundation stands with advocates supporting Ryder’s Law and efforts to end the horse-drawn carriage industry in New York City.

We believe there is a difference between honoring history and preserving practices that may no longer reflect modern standards of equine welfare.

Today, our thoughts are with Deniz, and every horse who has died on the streets of New York.

#ryderslaw #carriagehorses #endhorsedrawncarriages
